land.text: six of the seven Trucial sheikhdoms: Abu Dhabi, Ajman, Dubai, Fujairah, Sharjah and Umm Al Quwain

predecessors.note: Ras al-Khaimah, the seventh, joined in 1972 (ledger).

capitals.name: Abu Dhabi
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital: Abu Dhabi'. Coordinates from the gazetteer's place list.

correction.text: the six emirates of 2 December 1971, without Ras al-Khaimah

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the last month of 1971, before Cliopatria's row (1973): 'six of the emirates (Abu Dhabi, Ajman, Dubai, Fujairah, Sharjah, and Umm Al Quwain) agreed to enter into a union' on 2 December 1971; Ras al-Khaimah was not yet in. The shape is the 1973 shape less the Ras al-Khaimah emirate.

correction.text: all seven emirates, with Ras al-Khaimah

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1972: Ras al-Khaimah joined that year ('joined later, on 10 January 1972' in the text, '10 February 1972' in the infobox), so all seven emirates are in. The shape is Cliopatria's 1973 shape.

77,581 km2 for 1973-2023 against the infobox's 83,600 km2 (ratio 0.93; the page gives no year for it). The shape is the seven emirates; by the gazetteer it takes 13 edge cells in Oman (3,288 km2) and 7 in Saudi Arabia (1,770 km2) and misses 5 cells of the coast (1,264 km2) of the Natural Earth country: cells along frontiers that the page says were agreed with Saudi Arabia in 1974 ('formally demarcating the frontiers', not ratified) and with Oman (ratified in 2008); the overlap is outline noise, not a claim. The three islands Iran took on 30 November 1971 are smaller than a cell and not in the shape.
77,581 km2, the same outline for 2024 (ratio 0.93). No border change on the page for the final year.

region.text: the six emirates that agreed to the union, with Abu Dhabi as capital

ledger.note: 2 December 1971: six emirates form the United Arab Emirates. 'Six of the emirates (Abu Dhabi, Ajman, Dubai, Fujairah, Sharjah, and Umm Al Quwain) agreed to enter into a union'; infobox 'Independence from the United Kingdom: 2 December 1971', ending the British protectorate of the Trucial States.

region.text: the emirate of Ras al-Khaimah, the seventh

ledger.note: 1972: Ras al-Khaimah joins the federation. It 'joined later, on 10 January 1972' (text) or '10 February 1972' (infobox); the page disagrees with itself on the month, so only the year is given here.

wars.name: Iranian occupation of Abu Musa and the Tunbs

zones.text: Abu Musa, Greater Tunb and Lesser Tunb

wars.outcome: Iran took the islands by force on 30 November 1971; Abu Musa was leased to Iran and the page calls the UAE's claim unresolved.
wars.note: The title is the page's sentence, not an article opened; the occupation continues under the Islamic Republic (islamic-republic-of-iran) after 1979.

wars.name: 2011 military intervention in Libya
wars.outcome: The UAE 'joined international military operations in Libya in March 2011' and later supported Khalifa Haftar's Libyan National Army; the page gives no territorial result.
wars.note: Zones are empty: the page describes air deployments, not ground held.

wars.name: Saudi-led intervention in Yemen
wars.outcome: UAE forces fought in Yemen from 2015 (52 soldiers died in the Marib attack of 4 September 2015) with 'ground troop deployment in Southern Yemen'; the page does not say the UAE controls any territory abroad.
wars.note: Socotra, Mayun/Perim and Aden are not on the page, so no occupation is recorded.

certainty.note: The Saudi frontier was agreed in 1974 but 'has not been ratified'; the Oman frontier was ratified only in 2008; the Khor Al Adaid on the Qatar border is 'a source of ongoing dispute'; the islands taken by Iran in 1971 are claimed.
The Oman border is ratified (2008). The unratified Saudi agreement of 1974 and the Khor Al Adaid claim remain exceptions, and the islands held by Iran are still claimed.

sources.title: United Arab Emirates
sources.note: The only page opened (budget 1-2): infobox area 83,600 km2 and capital, 2 December 1971 union, Ras al-Khaimah 1972, Iranian seizure of the islands 30 November 1971, the 1974 Saudi agreement, Oman 2008, the Yemen and Libya deployments.

notes: Written by me-10-l on 2026-10-25 from one page (the Wikipedia article). Cliopatria's row begins in 1973; the state began on 2 December 1971 with six emirates, hence two new keyframes (1971, 1972). Ras al-Khaimah's accession date is inconsistent on the page (10 January vs 10 February 1972); the dossier keeps the year. The counterpart 'Ras al-Khaimah' is a sheikhdom named by the page; the trucial-states dossier ends in December 1971 without it, so a gap-filler may want a Ras al-Khaimah entry. ISLANDS: the 30 November 1971 seizure happened two days before this state existed; it is the Trucial States' loss and the Pahlavi dynasty's gain in those dossiers (Iran under the Islamic Republic from 1979 holds them), so this ledger has no event for it; the UAE's claim stands in certainty and in the war entry. Reviewer me-10-l removed the occupation_start of 30 November 1971 that this dossier carried, because it fell before the state's start and drew hatch on land outside its shape. The page does not say which emirate owned which island. Place names Abu Musa, Greater Tunb and Lesser Tunb are not in the gazetteer. BORDERS: the page says the 1974 Saudi agreement 'formally demarcating the frontiers' 'has not been ratified' and does not name the Treaty of Jeddah in its text; it names no land changing hands, so no gain/loss is recorded against Saudi Arabia or Oman. The Buraimi dispute (1955) is older than the state. NOT OPENED (page budget): the Trucial States and Abu Musa articles, which a gap-filler could use to date the emirates' pre-1971 claims.
